title: Does the missing-doublet pattern resemble a lag-one filter?
question: Does the unsolved LP2 stream distinguish a continuous lag-one repeat filter from tested recency, rebalancing and line-reset controls calibrated to the same repeat rate?
reader_question: Was the repeat-avoidance rule applied to the whole rune stream?
summary: The 86 residual adjacent repeats match a continuous lag-one-only filter better than the tested recency/rebalancing or line-reset controls. The comparison cannot distinguish computer code from a person applying the identical rule to otherwise machine-like symbols.
finding: Independent input measurements reproduce the 86/12,955 lag-one repeat rate, 3.488% lag-2–8 equality, 0.936 window-58 chi-square per degree of freedom, and 4/86 line-crossing repeats. In the source's 200-replicate matched-control ladder, models with extra recent-symbol avoidance or window rebalancing are distinguishable and rejected; the line-reset model is also distinguishable and rejected. The no-extra-effect hand rung has combined discrimination power 0.110 and remains unresolved.
limitations: This is a bounded comparison among specified generators, not proof of a literal machine implementation or entropy source. Controls are calibrated to the observed adjacent-repeat rate. The model ladder does not cover every human strategy; a continuous hand-applied lag-one rule on machine-like symbols is observationally equivalent here. The source counts 648 occupied slash/page line ordinals, whereas the text contains 594 nonempty physical lines.
next_steps: A proposed alternative filter should generate streams with the same lag-one repeat rate and declare its lag profile, window balance, line-boundary behavior and power before comparing with LP2.

scope.representation: First 55 nonempty percentage-delimited LP2 segments of pinned UTF-8 rune transcription, concatenated in page order; slash and page markers retained for line-scope comparisons. 12,956 runes, 55 pages, 594 nonempty physical lines, 648 occupied source line ordinals.
scope.procedure: Independently parse raw runes and reproduce lag equalities, repeat gaps, window chi-square, line-crossing doublets and page dispersion. Freshly run the pinned source fingerprint/controls script with 200 replicates, all controls calibrated to the manuscript lag-one repeat rate, and verify its gate, powered model ladder and scope test.
scope.parameters: 29-rune alphabet; lags 1–8; windows 29/58/116/290; 200 source replicates per modeled family; six hand-model rungs plus uniform, continuous filter and line-reset controls; acceptance interval central 95%; minimum discriminator power 0.80.
scope.exclusions: Other transcription layers, alternative human or machine generators not in the source ladder, an exact cipher/key, the physical identity of the author or pad entropy source.

review.reviewer: Independent raw-transcript count, lag/gap/window/line computation and fixed-seed source-control replay

reproduction.environment: Python 3; bundled source transcript and source receipts; NumPy required for original 200-replicate replay.

visuals.caption: The manuscript aligns with the matched continuous lag-one control on window balance and line-crossing doublets.

pages_note: 55 nonempty transcription pages: LP2-00–49 and LP2-51–55. The blank LP2-50 segment contributes no runes.
